transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Iris Long (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (Head of Security, Stellar Health), Dr. Miles Carter (CTO), Aisha Khan (DevOps), Rahul Menon (Legal)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery to evaluate Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for Stellar Health; primary concerns: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and least privilege, audit logs & retention, encryption and KMS/HSM options, data residency and retention policy, legal/contract constraints. Agreement to follow up with SOC2/ISO docs, SAML guide, Dedicated pricing, and schedule POC deep-dive.

Topics:
- Compliance evidence (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001)
- Authentication (SSO/SAML, SCIM, SAML metadata)
- Authorization (RBAC, least privilege, admin separation)
- Auditability (audit logs, log retention, tamper-evidence)
- Encryption (in transit, at rest, KMS/HSM integration)
- Deployment choices (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC/on-prem)
- Data residency and retention policies

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: all right, good afternoon everyone uh thanks for joining. this is Maya from Redwood along with Samir and Iris. how are you all doing?
[00:08] Lena: good thanks, thanks. um quick note we're on a bit of a timebox, we have a leadership sync afterwards so appreciate the efficiency.
[00:14] Maya: totally. quick goal for today is to understand Stellar's security requirements and where we'd fit - hosted v dedicated v private, and capture any blockers for procurement/legal.
[00:23] Dr. Carter: yeah we're evaluating options, primary thing is data residency and auditability - we process PHI-adjacent data so need clear controls.
[00:31] Samir: got it. when you say PHI-adjacent, can you give an example of workflows? like do you send raw transcripts offsite, or is it pseudonymized first?
[00:40] Aisha: currently we strip PII in upstream ETL for some workloads, but for others the call text flows to a downstream service for enrichment before de-id. so we need both network controls and strong access controls.
[00:52] Maya: great, that maps to the three main levers we typically discuss: network isolation (VPC / private), admin & RBAC controls, and data handling (encryption, retention, logs).
[01:02] Rahul: and on the legal side, we need to see SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary early, also contract language for data processing and sub-processors.
[01:10] Maya: absolutely, we'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 summary. I'll note that as an action item.
[01:16] Lena: perfect. can you summarize the difference between hosted and dedicated in security terms? there are some things i read in the deck but want clarity.
[01:25] Samir: sure, short version: Hosted is multi-tenant, Redwood manages the control plane and hardware; we offer strong encryption in transit and at rest, SOC 2 controls, and tenant separation. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and stronger data isolation - your workloads run on a committed fleet, and we can restrict network egress and provide per-customer VPC peering. Private packages go further: private control plane / on-prem options where you manage network and keys.
[01:48] Lena: do you offer HSM-backed keys or can we bring our own KMS?
[01:53] Samir: both. for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS integrations, and we can integrate with cloud HSMs. Hosted supports envelope encryption with customer KMS as an option for enterprise customers.
[02:04] Dr. Carter: and for audit logs, how granular are they? we need user-level actions, model inference requests, and admin role changes. retention needs to be at least 1 year, preferably 3.
[02:14] Samir: audit logs capture API calls, user activity, role changes, and per-request metadata like model_id, latency, and tokens. retention depends on plan; by default hosted keeps 90 days, but enterprise plans and Dedicated can extend retention (we can do 1-3 years).
[02:28] Aisha: how are logs stored? are they tamper-evident? can we stream to our SIEM?
[02:33] Maya: yes, logs can be exported via secure syslog/S3 to your SIEM. for Dedicated/Private we can provide write-once storage patterns and attestations; for tamper-evidence we have integrations to ship signed logs to your audit pipeline.
[02:46] Rahul: on SSO, we use Okta and require SAML 2.0 + SCIM provisioning; need role mapping and ability to limit admin roles. do you support that?
[02:56] Samir: yes, we support SAML for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC supports custom roles and least-privilege. mapping from Okta groups to Redwood roles is supported and we can provide sample SAML metadata and attribute mapping docs.
[03:08] Lena: what's the typical friction points for SAML setup? any gotchas?
[03:13] Samir: mostly metadata mismatch or certificate expiration; also group sync timing if you rely on SCIM for deprovisioning. we'll share a checklist.
[03:21] Maya: quick question on retention: is there any way to redact or purge historical data on demand? for example, if a user requests deletion under some privacy law.
[03:29] Samir: yes, on Dedicated/Private you can request account-level deletion or per-customer retention policies; we also have API-based deletion requests and retention windows. for Hosted we have processes but need legal sign-off on retention overrides.
[03:41] Aisha: for the POC we'd like to test VPC peering and sample throughput - around 100 qps peak, average 20 qps, latency SLO 150ms p95. do you have customers at those numbers on Dedicated?
[03:54] Samir: yes, Dedicated tiers can be sized for that. we'll prepare an estimated capacity plan. note that latency depends on model choice and quantization - 150ms p95 is challenging for some large models, but with optimized kernels and batching we can get close for smaller context models.
[04:10] Dr. Carter: cost is also a factor; if we go Dedicated we need predictable pricing commitments.
[04:15] Maya: understood - we'll include reserved capacity pricing and options for burst capacity.
[04:19] Lena: on encryption at rest, if we bring our own KMS, do you store plaintext anywhere in your control plane?
[04:25] Samir: no, keys never leave your KMS. data keys are envelope-encrypted; control plane metadata is minimal and can be encrypted. with Private/on-prem, you control the entire key lifecycle.
[04:36] Rahul: legal needs to see sub-processor list and a standard DPA.
[04:40] Maya: we'll attach our sub-processor list and a redlined DPA template, yes.
[04:44] Lena: one more - RBAC separation: can we have separate admin for billing vs model deployment?
[04:50] Samir: yes, we have role separation for billing, deployments, and security. custom roles let you scope permissions to routes, models, and projects.
[04:59] Aisha: operational question - if an engineer needs access to logs for debugging, can we grant short-lived access tokens?
[05:05] Samir: yes, we support short-lived tokens and session-based role elevation for sensitive access. SCIM deprovisioning is immediate for user revocation.
[05:13] Dr. Carter: what's your incident response like? SLAs for incident notification?
[05:17] Iris: we have standard incident response playbooks; for enterprise contracts we commit to notification timelines and post-incident reports. we'll share our IR checklist and contact matrix.
[05:25] Lena: curious about data residency - we operate in EU and US; can we ensure data stays in region?
[05:30] Samir: yes, we offer region pinning for data and model serving. Dedicated and Private give stronger guarantees; hosted can enforce region constraints for enterprise customers with contractual commitments.
[05:40] Rahul: any external pen tests or third-party attestation?
[05:43] Maya: we run third-party pen tests annually and will share summary findings; SOC2 report includes control testing.
[05:49] Lena: ok, this is helpful. next steps?
[05:52] Maya: recap - we'll send SOC2 and ISO docs, SAML metadata and SCIM guide, Dedicated pricing and capacity estimate, and sample network diagram. Samir will schedule a technical deep-dive POC to test VPC peering and throughput. Aisha will share current network egress rules. Lena will prioritize compliance items and Rahul will provide contract constraints.
[06:10] Dr. Carter: timeline - we'd like a POC in the next 3 weeks if possible.
[06:14] Maya: sounds reasonable; we'll try for a slot. any other blockers?
[06:18] Lena: nothing else from me. thanks.
[06:21] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up by EOD with the doc deck and action items.

End of transcript.
